stem: At a terminal, Route A jeepneys leave every 12 minutes and Route B jeepneys leave every 18 minutes. One of each leaves together at 6:00 a.m. At what time will both routes next leave together?
hints: The departures repeat, and you want the first time they happen together again. Is that the GCF or the LCM?
List the departure times in minutes after 6:00. Route A: 12, 24, … Route B: 18, … Keep going until a number shows up in both lists.
Find the smallest number on both lists. Add that many minutes to 6:00 a.m.

solution.methodName: LCM for things that repeat and meet again

steps.action: Things that repeat and meet again call for the LCM (least common multiple) of 12 and 18.
steps.why: Route A leaves at multiples of 12 minutes and Route B at multiples of 18. We want the first time that is a multiple of both.

steps.action: List multiples of the bigger number, 18: 18, 36, 54, …
steps.why: Listing the bigger number's multiples is faster. Then check each one against 12.

steps.action: 18 ÷ 12 is not a whole number, so 18 does not work.
36 ÷ 12 = 3, a whole number. So the LCM is 36 minutes.
Both routes next leave together at 6:36 a.m.

This adds 6 minutes, the GCF of 12 and 18. The GCF is for splitting into equal parts. For things that meet again, use the LCM.
This adds 12 + 18 = 30 minutes. But 30 is not a multiple of 12 or of 18, so neither route leaves at 6:30.
This adds 12 × 18 = 216 minutes (3 hours 36 minutes). They do leave together then, but they already did at 6:36.
